clue.text: Judge those acting foolishly have a point

parts.note: people who behave foolishly are asses
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A judge complains that the fools in court have a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge something is to evaluate or appraise it.

clue.text: Flat broke — meant to keep a bit

indicators.note: to keep means the rearranged letters hold another piece within them
broke suggests something smashed, so the letters of meant are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a bit is a part

explanation.surface: Someone who is broke intended to hang on to a little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat broke' reads as one phrase meaning penniless, but the clue splits after 'Flat': 'broke' is the anagram signal, and the bit kept goes in after the first letter of AMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is the British word for a self-contained set of rooms, an apartment.

clue.text: Shuffle along quiet promenade

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
to promenade is to stroll at leisure, to amble

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles quietly along the seafront promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: To shamble is to walk with a shuffling, awkward gait.

clue.text: Craftsman giving odd names to son

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of names to son are set out in a strange order

explanation.surface: A craftsman gives his son some peculiar names.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a skilled worker who cuts and dresses building stone.

clue.text: The sound of a snake that's been provoked

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
someone provoked is angry, irate

explanation.surface: The hiss made by an angry snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hiss, but the sound defined is the breathy H sound in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics an aspirate is a breathed consonant, the H sound.

clue.text: Frightened about non-drinking direction being broadcast

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the pieces that follow

parts.note: frightened means scared
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol
E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Panic spreads as an order banning drink is broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed that is broadcast is sown by flinging it widely, so it is scattered.

clue.text: I dry' up in exchange for sweets

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for dry is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sec is the French and wine-list word for dry

explanation.surface: Someone offers to dry the dishes in return for sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests drying dishes for a reward; 'dry' is the wine-list word, and the stray apostrophe after it is an OCR error, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ices are frozen desserts, a kind of sweet course.

clue.text: It's so hard for a worker after a stoppage

indicators.note: after means the worker comes behind the stoppage in the answer

parts.note: a dam stops a flow of water
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A worker finds things tough after a strike stops work.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant is a legendary stone of unbreakable hardness, so the clue calls it something so hard.

clue.text: Each single woman is on the track!

indicators.note: in a down clue being on means sitting above the next piece

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, stands for a woman
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the track

explanation.surface: Every unattached woman is out on the running track.
explanation.definitionFit: Every means all of a group taken one by one, each single member.

clue.text: The hide collapsed

definitions.meaning: an old word for an animal's skin or pelt
the past tense of fall, to come down suddenly

explanation.definitionFit: Fell means an animal skin, and fell is the past of fall, collapse.

clue.text: Shellfish needs salt only

parts.note: a salt is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is a sailor
only means alone

explanation.surface: A shellfish needs nothing but salt to cook it.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail with an ear-shaped shell.

clue.text: It is usual to declare date of birth

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly, declare
one's age is reckoned from one's date of birth

explanation.surface: Giving your date of birth is a standard requirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means typical or ordinary, what is normal.

clue.text: A spread for the board

parts.note: the spread seems to be a meal laid on a table, but it is the fabric spread over the dining board

explanation.definitionFit: This linen is spread over a dining table, which is also called the board.

clue.text: A lot of people get married, no matter what

parts.note: any means whichever one, no matter what

explanation.surface: Lots of people get married regardless of circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a pronoun, many means a large number of persons.

clue.text: The sorry outcome of error

parts.note: sorry seems to mean regrettable, but here it means penitent: the remorse felt after doing wrong

explanation.definitionFit: Contrition is sincere remorse that follows wrongdoing.

clue.text: See why a change would make nonsense

indicators.note: a change means the letters of see why a are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a change would be needed, calling it nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is slang for humbug or talk meant to deceive, rubbish.

clue.text: She dreads organising capital investment

indicators.note: organising means arranging, so the letters of she dreads are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman dreads having to arrange capital investment for a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital investment' sounds financial, but capital is the head and investment is clothing (being invested in robes).
explanation.definitionFit: A headdress is decorative covering worn on the head, which crosswords call the capital.

clue.text: The early caller wants a roll with no filling

indicators.note: filling means the nought goes into the middle of the list

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, a roster
O, a zero, means none

explanation.surface: An early visitor wants a bread roll without any filling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for an empty roll, but 'no filling' means the O for nothing is the filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel crows at dawn, so it is the first to call each morning.

clue.text: Check coaches among others

indicators.note: among means set in the middle of the other word

parts.note: the rest means the others
coaches are railway carriages, which together make a train

explanation.surface: A check is made on coaches among other vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is holding back, keeping something in check.

clue.text: Sort of pudding for a top CIA assemblage

indicators.note: an assemblage is something put together, so the letters of a top CIA are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A dessert gathering laid on for senior American spies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starchy grain from cassava, cooked with milk as a dessert.

clue.text: Head holding cheat to get proof

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the second

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
to rob is to cheat or defraud

explanation.surface: A headteacher holds a cheating pupil to get evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Probate is the legal proving of a will before its executors may act.

clue.text: Bodies found in docks

definitions.meaning: small bodies of soldiers assigned to a particular task
to dock an animal is to cut off its tail

explanation.surface: Corpses are discovered down at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Military details are small groups of troops; and docking removes tails.

clue.text: Some retain ten, several rather more, which is great!

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Keeping ten, and even more of several, would be a great result.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the end of 'retain' and ends early in 'several'.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means extreme in degree, very strong or great.

clue.text: Steer youngsters round the other way

indicators.note: round the other way means the word for youngsters is read backwards

parts.note: tots are small children

explanation.surface: Turn the children round to face the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb meaning guide, but it is the noun, a young bullock; a stot is a dialect word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A stot is a young castrated bullock, a steer.

clue.text: Passed a writer in the street

indicators.note: in means the writer goes inside the street

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An author went past in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up, exhausted, as time that has passed.

clue.text: Manage a number with little rest somehow

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a number
mini means small or little

indicators.note: somehow suggests the word rest must be rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: Organise a few people with a bit of rest in some fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer something is to run or direct it.

clue.text: Within the church — but not for long

parts.note: within means in
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A visitor stays inside the church only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not for long' sounds like time, but here it is a short distance.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a tiny length, so it is a measure of something short.

clue.text: A person making misrepresentation upsets the bar

indicators.note: in a down clue upsets means the word for bar is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: A fibber causes trouble in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A liar is someone who tells untruths.

clue.text: Getting out of a colliery to study -

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of
a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A student leaves the pit to study instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to inspect and study it closely.

clue.text: A Greek character not favouring Italian wine

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means opposed, not in favour

explanation.surface: A Greek dislikes the wine of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany.

clue.text: Project a man has become involved in to gain advancement

indicators.note: has become involved in means the man is placed inside the word to

parts.note: taken as written
he is a male pronoun, a man
a rise is a promotion or advancement

explanation.surface: A man has joined a project to win promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' looks like a noun, but it is a verb, to form ideas or speculate.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to speculate or project ideas about what may be the case.

clue.text: Requisition during the depression

parts.note: in means during, as in the morning
a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: An order issued during the economic slump.
explanation.definitionFit: An indent is an official order for goods or stores, a requisition.
